summary_overview: Confluent Developer talk arguing that prompt engineering is dead — context is king. With at most ~1M tokens in the context window, you must fit everything the LLM needs: business knowledge, goals, tools, resources. The speaker lays out six components of context: user message, system prompt, tools, resources, assistant messages, and tool call history. The latter three grow as the agent runs. More context is not always better — 60–70% of the context window often yields best results. Four engineering tools: (1) System prompt — balance vague vs prescriptive; define outcomes, not if-then logic. (2) Tool descriptions — specific, with full schemas. (3) Data retrieval — RAG works but MCP enables the LLM to decide which resources to fetch; describe what is available and let the model request what it needs. (4) Long-horizon thinking — compaction (summarize large resources), memory (key-value store for intermediate results), and agent composition (split complex logic into sub-agents). Context engineering is the present and future of agentic AI.
